Great game that builds on the systems and ideas laid by L4D. While the basic setup is the same (semi-randomized item and enemy spawns, hordes of weak enemies with special ones thrown in for a challenge, built around 4 people co-op) it does add a lot of variety by having different classes, builds, weapon type variety and the loot system makes it an overall more compelling experience over time since it has a lot more variety in how you can play.

Shame everyone in matchmaking fucking sucks at the game.

endless loop of stabbing, shooting and running in circles. i can see how it would be fun to certain people, but playing the same missions over and over again to get slightly better gear isnt the game play loop i want. fun enough to play with a group of friends if you just want to run around hitting your mouse button, stabbing and slashing things to no end. character classes lack true diversity in any meaningful way. play whoever you want because its all the same poke and shoot game play. finding the grimoires on each map is a slog, especially if youre playing with randoms that dont give a damn. you go down and the grimoire is lost forever because your teammates are running forwards at full speed and couldnt get back to you even if they wanted to because the map is full of ledges you cant get back up. i will admit that for being an older game, it is still better than a lot of the slop AAA companies are pushing out. i would not recommend this game if youre looking for something to play by yourself or randoms. do purchase if you have a group of 3 or 4 people as playing in a party is the only thing that might redeem this game

If you loved Vermintide 1, this entirely worthy sequel is a must-play. Fatshark have fiddled under the hood with a lot of things, but the end result is the sublime co-op goodness that made the first game such a stand-out. You get the same constantly evolving tactical puzzles thanks to the clever AI director, and the same ridiculously deep combat mechanics that will reward your attention and patience.

What's truly new in Vermintide 2 is the expansive and beautiful level design. The maps from the first game feel tiny and cramped by comparison, just the new ones are so vast and sweeping. They feel even more like real locations tied up in an epic struggle between good and evil.

Vermintide 2 is deeply engaging and beautiful out of the gate, and with official modding support and new patches and DLC planned for years to come, this game is only going to get even better. Highly recommended!

The combat is very visceral. The game keeps you on your toes constantly. The classes ("careers") are different enough to make switching around and trying things fun. The banter between the characters is top notch, both writing and voice acting.

Vermintide 2 might be the very best "AI Director" co-op game of all time.
In hindsight, it released in that goldilocks era just before the over-monetization kicked in. And it cut it *really* close. All maps and mission-like content is free, but a cash shop for cosmetics was patched in later. Even got DLC player classes, but I personally was happy to support the game and did pay for that bundle. Only other $$ I spent on the game.

The idea that I can relaunch the game in 2026, after more than a 5 year gap, and not just be presented with new content to conquer, but for the game to still feel as incredibly polished as it does, is astounding. Even the player population seems to be fine somehow.
(I have not dove into the new-ish PvP mode, so idk how active that scene is. But the fact that I even need to make that caveat is incredible)

Seriously, if you want to play a co-op horde clearing game where every ding of HP feels as fair as it gets in the genre, this is it. Keep your ears peeled for those audio cues, because there's no modern babymode cheaty systems like foes only attacking when they are in your FoV.

This is a great Co-Op game. If you like Left 4 Dead style game play, this is a great game to pick up. Lot's of weapon options, class variations and fun levels. Not to mention the challenging skill levels as you progress.

Do note, for anybody reading this, that while this game is amazing and I thoroughly enjoy it, your first 10ish hours are going to be boring as hell. This game gets more enjoyable the more you learn every mechanic, deal with every increasing odds of enemies, and play with other people of similar skill levels where you all have each other's backs in stressful situations. The devs of this game appear to have tailors things to be this way, and it's a blast! That is if you can get past the early first few hours. Playing on the first two difficulties is a fucking snore, you will be bonking at max 10 enemies at a time and you'll see like a single special/monster per level. You are stuck in these lower snorefest difficulties until you level up and get better gear, which while not taking too long is still a bore that prevents you from playing the actual fun parts of the game. If you're looking to get this game, then I would recommend you find a friend to level up with at the start and once you get your first character to level 30 and are playing at the very least champion difficulty, you can finally start having fun.

Instead of fixing game breaking bugs and paying attention to balance, the team puts up cosmetics for sale.

Multiplayer is super smooth, really fast connection and loading times for lobbies. Fun co-op, lots of different modes to try. Can't wait to try them all! There's some stuttering when using voice chat - game is very smooth 100% of the time otherwise. Good optimization!

I love the expeditions - randomized mini-campaigns with decent rewards, with all team members starting with base-level equipment and upgrading with coins found throughout the campaign. Great Rogue-lite experience!

It's also kinda easy to get all the achievements, all you have to do it's just to play the game I got all of them in 84 hours

Horde-style fps games are probably my favorite genre of video game. L4D2, DRG, Risk of Rain, DOOM Eternal; I just love slaughtering a lot of guys at once, with specials and unique enemy types thrown in. Vermintide II scratches that itch horde-slaying itch in just the right way. It's faced-paced, it's violent, it has fantastic music, art direction, level design, and voice acting. Learning weapon combos and using them to absolutely melt hordes of filthy rats and Nurgle worshipers is immensely satisfying.

My only major gripe is with overall progression. Overall, it's not terribly satisfying. All upgrades to both gear and talents are typically small percentage increases. You will never unlock a new ability for a career, you will never see a huge increase to your stats. It is a slow burn of a progression system that works for what it is, but could feel more rewarding with more prevalent upgrades and unlockable abilities.

Would highly recommend this game if you have a few friends to play with. Solo/quickplay is fine, but this game really shines when everyone is communicating, making calls, playing to their role, and goofing off.
The graphics are insane and the ragdoll is really fun, also its brutal seeing a rat get his brain splattered by an attack. really good game, worth the buy.

The best Coop game I have played since L4D2, interesting story orientated missions and hard difficulty levels that offer challenges that last for hundreds of hours playtime.
Community is great, gave me a good first entry into the Warhammer fantasy universe and is just a well rounded game.
Classes are diverse and everyone usually finds their favourite career quickly.
Fatshark is now a reputable developer who will hopefully pull another great stunt with Darktide.

It's a good vent for a bad day, just mindless warhammer slaughter at it's finest - that being said ; if you've had a really bad day, it may tip you over the edge to screen smashing and rage if you play solo because even on "recruit" difficulty it can be difficult if you're carelessly wading into swarms.
This is like Left 4 Dead 2 but Medieval/Steampunk! It features 5 different characters with 4 man teams. You fight against cults of Rats and Northerners to protect your country!

Grab some friends, bash some skulls. Vermintide 2 is good fun. Playing with random players online is a mixed bag because some people lack basic communication competencies and ruin a round but thankfully it doesn't take long to get another one going. Playing with NPCs is serviceable but won't get you through the higher difficulties.
The five playable characters are cool and varied and the subclasses provide even more variety. As for the five DLC classes, maybe wait for a sale for those.
The look system will bug many people and I'll admit, it still annoys me but it's usually not a major concern.

The Chaos Wastes update is where the game really got a new shine for me, because the almost roguelite nature of this mode is really cool too.

Yes-yes, listen-hear me, man-thing.
This game is good-great. Too good, maybe. The graphics are shiny-pretty, the combat is fast-choppy, and smashing rat skulls never gets old-boring.
The heroes are strange-funny, always talking-arguing while thousands of superior Skaven warriors heroically throw themselves into their blades. Such sacrifice. Much tragedy.
The story is interesting enough to keep the slaughter moving, but the real joy comes from carving a path through endless hordes of rat-things, beast-things, and other unfortunate creatures.
The gameplay is smooth-smooth, the mechanics are excellent, and every mission somehow turns into complete chaos-disaster in the best possible way.
Buy-acquire this game, yes-yes. Especially if it is on sale. Few things in life are worth more than hearing "RAT OGRE!" moments before your entire team dies horribly.
10/10. Would exterminate-kill my fellow Skaven again. Yes-yes. 🐀🐀🐀
A beautifully dark fantasy setting, a merry band of characters and an awesome fighting system. This game will suck you in if you let it!

Among all the first person co-op hack n slash games out there, this one stands alone as the best there is.

If you wanna chop up waves and waves of enemies while leveling characters and hoarding loot, accept no substitutes.

There are many FPS games, there are many RPG hack n slash games, but there's only one Vermintide 2.

.... ok so maybe that actually means there's been two vermintides, whatever, shut up and buy it.

Contains Red Shell Spyware

Red shell is a Spyware that tracks data of your PC and shares it with 3rd parties. On their website they formulate it all in very harmless language, but the fact is that this is software from someone i don't trust and whom i never invited, which is looking at my data and running on my pc against my will. This should have no place in a full price PC game, and in no games if it were up to me.

Red Shell can collect the following to create a 'fingerprint' unique identifier for your computer:

Your Gamer tag (Steam, Xbox live, PSN, etc) may be used

Redshell also mentions that they do/have collect ip addresses

Operating System (e.g., Windows 10, Windows 7, Mac OS X 10.11.5, Windows Vista Service Pack 2)

Screen Resolution (e.g., 1920x1080, 1440x900)

Timezone (Based on offsets of UTC)

Language (Your computer's language or region code, e.g., en, de, en-us, en-ca)

Installed Fonts (All fonts installed on the computer)

Installed Browsers (Names and version numbers)

Left 4 Dead in a fantasy setting. It could use more maps (they could work to import the maps from the first Vermintide but for some reason they don't). It desperately needs dedicated servers: I'm tired of noobs hosting the game, rushing alone and ragequitting as soon as they get downed. A great experience though if you have friends to play with or even with bots. It's often super cheap, it runs smoothly on old potato pcs and it looks pretty. Highly recommended.

To make this review get to the point as fast as possible:
The game is entirely carried by its gameplay.

That means that it is a lot of fun when you first boot it up, but once you have grown tired of the gameplay, this game becomes nothing more than a game you play one round in every 2 weeks or so to have a bit of fun.
And that is not bad, because this game is very fun, especially with friends.

Sadly, the game offers nothing more besides that. The actual story content of the story mode lasts 10 minutes max, most characters are quirky but nothing more, the levels are all gorgeous but frustratingly linear, and a lot of the game's systems feel underbaked. The most frustrating example is that while there is a leaderboard for kills, killing enemies (90% of the game) gives you no direct progression for your characters unless you complete some random challenge by accident.

Still, I would recommend this game, since it is on sale most of the time and can be very fun as long as you play it as a side game and do not expect too much.

I've been in this game since it was released, i was there during the great cleave nerf, and i came back for winds of magic. Although WoM had largely negative reviews, they fixed it all in the latest patch and it is now just as fun and engaging as this game has allways been. The devs actually do stuff and it seems they listen to the playerbase. I hope to see more DLCs and games from these guys in the future.

Since the release of this game I stayed away, thinking it wouldn't be much different than Vermintide 1. At some point last year (2018) I got a bit bored with Vermintide 1 and decided to read the reviews here. Several reviews had believable complaints of anti-cheat banning the gamer who claimed they didn't cheat.

During the recent free to play weekend I decided to jump in and play. WOW! I was so wrong in my assumptions of not being much different than Vermintide 1. The bosses/monsters speak adding to the atmosphere of the game, enemy types vary beyond the skaven in Vermintide 1 giving the game a different "feel". Character level progression as well as item progression is arguably better. Lastly the maps in my opinion are more diverse.

Personally it would be great if an additional character were added such as a Thief or Rogue like male or female character. Does anyone remember or know of Tasselhoff from the Dragonlance series of books.

This is a great game and in my opinion would be made even better if a DLC added PVP option in which 2 teams are pitted against each other and one team were the enemy type characters such as Left for Dead. It could be fun to spawn as an Assassin Rat (Hunter), Rat Gunner, Rat Ogre, Chaos Warrior, and etc.

Repetitive gameplay due to lootbox mechanics. You are forced to grind your character levels up to unlock talents (perks) and increase your "Hero Power" - which DIRECTLY affects your damage output; and grind for lootboxes which gradually drop better and better weapons.
You can obviously still try playing higher difficulties early on, but lets be honest, you are at a massive disadvantage when you can't kill enemies efficiently.

That brings me to the second point - Higher difficulties are just more and tougher enemies and specials being spawned, often to a level of complete bullshit because of RNG - on Legend difficulty, there were times when enemies could literally be so packed and crowded together, they superposed on each other; also, RNG allowed a swarm and specials being spawned while the whole team was fighting a boss enemy.
There were occasions that there was nothing the team could do. It was inconsistent and just not enjoyable.

There are 13 maps in the base campaign, a few DLC maps but that was it, unless you buy the DLCs. And there are so many times you can play the same maps over and over again to grind your level and lootboxes.

Sept 28, 2025: this game is officially toast now. only a few team-style players left in player base. Fatshark sub-contractor deliberately making game unplayable so they can stop sustaining the game. was a great game back in the day.

Dec 9, 2024: goodbye fatshark. never again.

this game is 6 years old. STILL has backend errors, lag TPK's, holes in the maps you fall through. It will never get fixed.

This game is very fun to play with friends and is not to hard to learn either. The grind never gets boring to me and each hero has its own play style to learn. I personally main Victor Saltzpyre, mostly the Witch Hunter and Warrior Priest of Sigmar. Even though the game has paid classes and Dlc it does not take away from the fun of the game. 10/10 would recommend.

I love this game. It's left 4 dead but with melee focused combat along with ranged weaponry and spells. It's better than the first game in terms of optimization. The loot system is also focused on the character you use rather than any possible character like the first game.

If you like games that are focused primarily on cooperation, PvE, and grinding the same maps for better gear that have endless hordes, bosses and special enemies that can appear (some in combination) then get this game! You won't regret it!
Great game! Annoying to have the monetization BS. If you can stand all that monetization loops and daily quests crap - can easily recommend.

I love this game... just wish I had more friends that played it on a regular basis who like to enjoy the game. Like many games, you end up in teams where someone runs ahead and wants to "optimize" the run and grind. Me, I like to just play each run like I've never played it before looking for art, tomes, and such. Kill every MOB I see. I like to just enjoy the run so I am often frowned upon or perceived as lagging behind when not playing with "real" friends. Regardless, it's a great game even with some of the downsides of playing with RANDS and not having enough gamer friends. It's a must have in your game library... always installed!

Very fun game. I dont even feelt like gaming much lately but this one been keeping me coming back. Seems to have a fair amount of replayability.

I do wish the story is a little bit longer for the future one, as a lot of the replayability and game modes seem more fit for when I was younger and liked grinding, as opposed to something more varied. But on sale, it's a steal.

One of my favorite games the past couple years. The melee combat is actually very nuanced, it's not just spam clicks, although you can do that. The different weapons have different combos and alternate abilities, which again adds a good bit of depth to the combat if you choose to explore it further. The world building in this game is second to none, and the immersion is absolutely incredible. The graphics are still great to this day and age - and even something as simple as iron end caps on spikes have their own set of textures, bringing a lot of thought and care to the detail of the warhammer world. Fatshark has undoubtedly struck gold with this game series, and I am eagerly hoping there is a 3rd. Looking forward to Darktide!
